title: What happened in AI — Oct 31–Nov 6, 2026
intro: Open-weight Kimi K3.1 Pro landed with day-0 serving from vLLM, Huawei Ascend and hosted providers, so launch-day infrastructure support is now part of a model release.
On the agent side, measurements said the harness matters more than the model: the same Haiku scored 82.0% or 65.4% depending on the agent, and a 17-agent setup lost to vanilla Claude Code.
Security followed: MCP servers, coding-tool browsers and stolen API keys were all exploited. Build controls around the tool call, not the prompt.
highlights: Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T MoE, 1M context) shipped open weights with day-0 vLLM and Ascend support.
Same model, different agent: 82.0% vs 65.4% across 21 MCP servers.
A planner/coder/reviewer team passed 25.7% of tests versus 56.8% for one Codex agent.
Mandiant: stolen LLM API keys produced nearly $1M in charges at one company.
An H200 loses money even fully busy; a B300 profits at 35% utilization.
